exercises.name: Chair squat
instructions: Stand tall in front of a sturdy chair with your feet a little wider than your hips and your toes turned slightly out.
Send your hips back and bend both knees, lowering slowly until your hips touch the chair.
Keep your chest facing forward and your whole foot in contact with the floor as you lower.
Press evenly through both feet to stand back up to full height, and finish standing tall before you step away from the chair.
cues: Let your knees travel in the same direction as your toes.
Touch the chair lightly rather than dropping onto it.

exercises.name: Dumbbell goblet squat
instructions: Hold a single dumbbell upright against your chest with both hands cupped under the top end.
Stand with your feet a little wider than your hips and your toes turned slightly out.
Send your hips back and bend your knees, lowering until your thighs are roughly parallel to the floor or until your heels want to lift, whichever comes first.
Drive through both feet to stand back up with the dumbbell still against your chest, and place it on the floor when you have finished.
cues: Keep your elbows tucked inside your knees at the bottom.
Keep your ribs stacked over your hips rather than leaning back.

exercises.name: Barbell back squat
instructions: Set the bar in a rack at about the height of your collarbone and step under it so the bar rests across the muscles at the top of your back, never on your neck.
Grip the bar evenly with both hands, stand up to lift it out of the rack, and take a short step back with each foot.
With your feet a little wider than your hips, send your hips back and bend your knees until your thighs are roughly parallel to the floor.
Drive through both feet to stand back up, then walk the bar forward into the rack hooks and let it settle before you step away.
cues: Keep the bar stacked over the middle of your feet throughout.
Ask gym staff to check your rack height and safety pins before you begin.

exercises.name: Leg press machine
instructions: Sit in the leg press with your back and hips flat against the padded support.
Place your feet flat on the platform about hip width apart and level with each other.
Release the safety catches, then bend your knees to let the platform travel towards you until your knees reach about a right angle.
Press the platform away until your legs are almost straight without locking your knees hard, and re-engage the catches before you climb out.
cues: Keep your lower back in contact with the pad the whole way down.
Stop lowering before your hips start to curl up off the seat.

exercises.name: Hip hinge to wall
instructions: Stand a short step in front of a wall with your back to it and your feet about hip width apart.
Rest your hands on the front of your thighs and keep a soft bend in your knees.
Push your hips straight back until they touch the wall, letting your chest tip forward and your hands slide down your thighs.
Squeeze your hips to stand back up to full height, and finish standing tall away from the wall.
cues: Move at the hips rather than rounding your upper back.
Keep your head in line with your chest as it tips forward.

exercises.name: Glute bridge
instructions: Lie on your back on a mat or carpet with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor beneath your knees.
Rest your arms alongside your body with your palms down.
Press through your heels and lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Lower your hips back to the floor under control, and finish lying flat before you get up.
cues: Lift with your hips rather than arching your lower back.
Keep your ribs down as your hips rise.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, palms facing you.
Soften your knees and keep them in that position for the whole movement.
Push your hips back and let the dumbbells travel down the front of your legs, stopping where you feel your hamstrings lengthen or where your back would otherwise round.
Squeeze your hips to stand back up to full height, then place the dumbbells on the floor when you have finished.
cues: Keep the dumbbells brushing close to your legs.
Let your hips travel back rather than your knees travel forward.

exercises.name: Barbell hip thrust
instructions: Sit on the floor with your upper back resting against the long edge of a flat bench and your knees bent, feet flat.
Roll a padded barbell over your hips so it sits across the crease at the top of your legs, and steady it with both hands.
Press through your heels and lift your hips until your body is level from your knees to your shoulders.
Lower your hips under control until they touch the floor, then roll the bar off before you stand up.
cues: Tuck your chin slightly so your eyes follow your hips.
Finish the lift with your hips level rather than arching your back.

exercises.name: Bodyweight split squat
instructions: Stand with one foot forward and the other a long stride behind you, with the back heel lifted.
Rest a hand on a wall or the back of a chair for balance if you need it.
Bend both knees to lower your back knee towards the floor, stopping just before it touches.
Press through your front foot to return to standing, work the other side the same way, and finish standing tall with both feet together.
cues: Keep your torso upright rather than leaning over your front knee.
Place your feet on slightly different lines so you are not balancing along a single line.

exercises.name: Bodyweight step up
instructions: Stand facing a stair or a low, stable step that does not move when you press on it.
Place your whole front foot on the step and rest a hand on a wall or rail for balance.
Press through the foot on the step to bring your body up until that leg is straight, then bring the other foot up to meet it.
Step back down with the same control, lead with the other leg for the same work, and finish standing on the floor.
cues: Push down through the step instead of hopping off the floor.
Choose a step height that lets your front heel stay flat.

exercises.name: Dumbbell split squat
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand by your sides and stand with one foot forward, the other a long stride behind, with the back heel lifted.
Place your feet on slightly different lines so you have a stable base.
Bend both knees to lower your back knee towards the floor, stopping just before it touches.
Press through your front foot to stand back up, work the other side the same way, and set the dumbbells down to finish.
cues: Keep your torso upright rather than leaning over the front knee.
Let your front heel stay flat on the floor throughout.

exercises.name: Dumbbell reverse lunge
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand by your sides and your feet under your hips.
Step one foot straight back and lower that knee towards the floor, keeping your front heel flat.
Stop just before your back knee touches, with both knees bent at about a right angle.
Press through your front foot to bring the back foot in beside the other, change legs, and set the dumbbells down to finish.
cues: Step back far enough that your front knee stays above your front foot.
Keep your chest facing forward rather than tipping towards the front knee.

exercises.name: Wall push up
instructions: Stand facing a wall, a little less than arm's length away, with your feet under your hips.
Place both palms on the wall at about chest height, a little wider than your shoulders.
Bend your elbows to bring your chest towards the wall, keeping your body in a straight line from your head to your heels.
Press the wall away until your arms are straight again, and finish by stepping back from the wall.
cues: Keep your hips in line with your shoulders rather than letting them sag.
Angle your elbows back rather than flaring them straight out to the sides.

exercises.name: Incline push up
instructions: Place both hands on a stable, waist-high surface such as a kitchen counter or a sturdy bench, a little wider than your shoulders.
Walk your feet back until your body is straight from your head to your heels and your weight rests on your hands and toes.
Bend your elbows to bring your chest towards the surface, stopping when your chest is close to it.
Press back up until your arms are straight, then walk your feet in and stand up to finish.
cues: Choose a higher surface if your hips begin to sag, a lower one if the movement feels easy.
Look at a point on the surface just ahead of your hands to keep your neck long.

exercises.name: Dumbbell floor press
instructions: Lie on your back on a mat with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Bring the dumbbells to the sides of your chest with your upper arms resting on the floor at a slight angle from your body.
Press both dumbbells straight up until your arms are almost straight above your chest.
Lower them under control until your upper arms touch the floor again, then place the dumbbells beside you before you sit up.
cues: Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows throughout.
Let the floor stop the movement rather than reaching for extra depth.

exercises.name: Barbell bench press
instructions: Lie on the bench with your eyes under the bar, your feet flat on the floor and your shoulder blades drawn down into the bench.
Grip the bar a little wider than your shoulders and lift it out of the hooks with straight arms.
Lower the bar under control to the middle of your chest, keeping your elbows angled slightly towards your body.
Press the bar back up over your shoulders, then guide it into the hooks and let it settle before you sit up.
cues: Ask a training partner or gym staff to stand behind the bar before you begin.
Keep both feet flat and still on the floor.

exercises.name: Chest press machine
instructions: Set the seat so the handles line up with the middle of your chest when you sit down.
Sit with your back flat against the pad and take a handle in each hand.
Press the handles forward until your arms are almost straight, without locking your elbows hard.
Let the handles travel back under control until your hands are level with your chest, then rest the stack down fully before you stand up.
cues: Keep your shoulders back against the pad as you press.
Move at an even speed in both directions.

exercises.name: Wall slide
instructions: Stand with your back against a wall and your feet a short step away from it.
Place the backs of your forearms and hands against the wall with your elbows bent to about a right angle.
Slide your arms up the wall as far as you can while keeping your forearms, wrists and lower back in contact with it.
Slide them back down to the starting position under control, and finish by stepping away from the wall.
cues: Stop sliding upward where your lower back starts to lift off the wall.
Keep your ribs down and your chin level.

exercises.name: Dumbbell overhead press
instructions: Stand with your feet under your hips holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing forward.
Brace your middle so your ribs stay stacked over your hips.
Press both dumbbells overhead until your arms are almost straight and the weights sit above your shoulders.
Lower them under control back to shoulder height, and place the dumbbells on the floor once you have finished.
cues: Move your head back slightly as the dumbbells pass your face, then return it.
Press upward rather than leaning back to help the weights up.

exercises.name: Barbell overhead press
instructions: Set the bar in a rack at about shoulder height and grip it a little wider than your shoulders.
Lift the bar out of the rack onto the front of your shoulders and take a short step back with each foot.
Press the bar overhead until your arms are almost straight and the bar sits above the middle of your feet.
Lower it under control to the front of your shoulders, then step forward and return the bar to the rack.
cues: Squeeze your hips and middle so your lower back does not arch.
Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows.

exercises.name: Prone reverse fly
instructions: Lie face down on a mat with your forehead resting on a folded towel and your arms out to the sides, palms down.
Draw your shoulder blades gently together and down.
Lift both hands a small distance off the floor with your arms almost straight and your neck relaxed.
Lower them back to the floor under control, and finish lying flat before you get up.
cues: Lead with the backs of your hands rather than shrugging your shoulders.
Keep your forehead resting on the towel throughout.

exercises.name: Resistance band seated row
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs straight in front of you and loop the middle of a resistance band around both feet.
Hold an end of the band in each hand with your arms straight and your back upright.
Draw both elbows back past your ribs, keeping them close to your body, until your hands reach the sides of your waist.
Let your arms straighten again under control, then release the tension from the band before you unhook your feet.
cues: Sit tall rather than leaning back to pull the band.
Start the pull from your shoulder blades, not from your hands.

exercises.name: Dumbbell single arm row
instructions: Place your left knee and left hand on a bench or sturdy chair so your back is roughly level with the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in your right hand with that arm straight below your shoulder.
Draw your right elbow back towards your hip until your hand reaches the side of your ribs.
Lower the dumbbell under control until your arm is straight, work the other side the same way, and set the dumbbell down to finish.
cues: Keep your shoulders level with each other as you pull.
Let your body stay still while only the arm moves.

exercises.name: Seated cable row machine
instructions: Sit facing the cable station with your feet on the platform and a slight bend in your knees.
Take the handle with both hands and sit upright with your arms straight.
Draw both elbows back past your ribs until your hands reach the front of your waist.
Let the handle travel forward under control until your arms are straight, then return the weight to the stack before you stand up.
cues: Keep your torso upright instead of rocking backward and forward.
Let your shoulder blades slide together as the handle comes in.

exercises.name: Resistance band lat pulldown
instructions: Anchor a resistance band securely above head height and kneel or sit facing the anchor.
Take an end of the band in each hand with your arms straight overhead and your body upright.
Pull both elbows down and out to the sides until your hands are level with your shoulders.
Let your arms straighten back overhead under control, then release the band's tension before you unhook it.
cues: Keep your upper body still and let your arms do the work.
Check that the anchor point holds before you take any tension.

exercises.name: Lat pulldown machine
instructions: Set the thigh pad so it holds your legs down when you sit, and choose a grip a little wider than your shoulders.
Sit down, take the bar with both hands and let your arms straighten overhead.
Pull the bar down in front of your face until it reaches the top of your chest, drawing your elbows towards your ribs.
Let the bar travel back up under control until your arms are straight, then guide it to its resting position before you stand up.
cues: Lean back only slightly and keep that angle for the whole movement.
Pull the bar in front of your head, never behind your neck.

exercises.name: Assisted pull up machine
instructions: Set the assistance level so you can complete the movement under control, then kneel or stand on the platform.
Take the handles above you with your arms straight and your shoulders drawn down away from your ears.
Pull your body up until your chin reaches the height of your hands.
Lower yourself under control until your arms are straight, then step off once the platform has come to a stop.
cues: Begin each pull by drawing your shoulder blades down.
Keep your body still rather than swinging for momentum.

exercises.name: Forearm plank
instructions: Lie face down on a mat and place your forearms on the floor with your elbows under your shoulders.
Tuck your toes under and lift your hips and knees off the floor so your body forms a straight line from your head to your heels.
Hold that position with your hips level, breathing steadily.
Lower your knees back to the floor to finish, then push yourself back to standing.
cues: Squeeze your hips and middle so your lower back stays flat.
Let your knees rest on the floor if your hips start to drop.

exercises.name: Dead bug
instructions: Lie on your back on a mat with both arms reaching straight up towards the ceiling.
Lift your knees so they sit above your hips with your shins parallel to the floor.
Press your lower back gently into the floor, then lower an arm overhead and the opposite leg towards the floor.
Bring them back to the start, work the other pair the same way, and finish lying flat before you get up.
cues: Stop lowering where your lower back would lift off the floor.
Breathe out slowly as your limbs travel away from you.

exercises.name: Incline forearm plank
instructions: Place both forearms on a stable, waist-high surface with your elbows under your shoulders.
Walk your feet back until your body forms a straight line from your head to your heels.
Hold that position with your hips level and your weight shared between your forearms and your toes.
Walk your feet back in and stand up to finish.
cues: Choose a higher surface if your hips begin to sag.
Keep your neck long by looking at the surface just ahead of your hands.

exercises.name: Bird dog
instructions: Kneel on a mat on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and your knees under your hips.
Set your back flat and your neck in line with it, looking at the floor.
Reach an arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are level with your body, without letting your hips tip.
Bring them back under you, change sides, and finish kneeling with both hands and knees on the mat.
cues: Keep your hips square to the floor as the leg travels back.
Reach long rather than lifting high.

exercises.name: Side plank
instructions: Lie on your side on a mat with your forearm on the floor, elbow under your shoulder, and your knees bent behind you.
Stack your hips and shoulders so your body forms a straight line from your head to your knees.
Lift your hips off the floor and hold that line, keeping your top shoulder above the bottom one.
Lower your hips back to the floor, change sides, and finish lying flat before you get up.
cues: Press the floor away with your forearm to keep your shoulder supported.
Straighten your legs instead of bending your knees when you want a harder version.

exercises.name: Resistance band Pallof press
instructions: Anchor a resistance band at about chest height and stand side on to the anchor, a short distance away.
Hold the band in both hands against the middle of your chest with your feet under your hips.
Press both hands straight out in front of you, resisting the band's pull towards the anchor.
Draw your hands back to your chest under control, turn to face the other way and work that side, then release the tension to finish.
cues: Keep your hips and shoulders facing forward the whole time.
Step further from the anchor for more tension, closer for less.

exercises.name: Dumbbell farmer carry
instructions: Stand between a pair of dumbbells placed on the floor beside your feet.
Bend at your hips and knees to take one in each hand, then stand up tall with your arms straight by your sides.
Walk forward in a straight line at an even pace, keeping your shoulders level and your ribs stacked over your hips.
Walk back to where you started, then bend your hips and knees to place the dumbbells on the floor.
cues: Take your normal stride length rather than rushing.
Keep your shoulders drawn back rather than letting the weight pull them forward.

exercises.name: Dumbbell suitcase carry
instructions: Stand beside a single dumbbell placed on the floor next to your right foot.
Bend at your hips and knees to pick it up in your right hand, then stand tall with that arm straight by your side.
Walk forward in a straight line, resisting the pull towards the loaded side so your shoulders stay level.
Walk back, place the dumbbell down, then carry out the same walk holding it in your left hand to finish.
cues: Keep both shoulders at the same height the whole way.
Let your free arm hang relaxed by your side rather than sticking it out.

exercises.name: Outdoor walk
instructions: Choose a flat, even route with good footing, and good lighting when it is dark.
Start walking at an easy pace and let your body warm up.
Build to a pace where your breathing is noticeably deeper but you could still speak in full sentences.
Ease back to the easy pace for the final stretch of the route and finish standing still until your breathing settles.
cues: Let your arms swing freely rather than holding them across your body.
Shorten the route or slow the pace whenever the walk stops feeling repeatable.

exercises.name: Marching in place
instructions: Stand tall in a clear space with your feet under your hips and your arms relaxed by your sides.
Lift a knee towards hip height, place that foot back down, then lift the other knee.
Swing your arms in an easy rhythm opposite to your legs as the pace picks up.
Slow the march gradually and finish standing still with both feet on the floor.
cues: Stay on the spot rather than drifting forward.
Lower each foot quietly so the movement stays smooth.

exercises.name: Treadmill walk
instructions: Step onto the treadmill belt and attach the safety clip to your clothing before you start the belt.
Start the belt at its slowest setting and let it move under you before you take your hands off the rail.
Raise the speed in small increments to a walking pace where your breathing is deeper but you could still speak in full sentences.
Lower the speed gradually, let the belt come to a stop, and step off once it has stopped completely.
cues: Walk in the middle of the belt rather than drifting towards the back.
Use the rail for balance only, not to carry your weight.

exercises.name: Stationary bike
instructions: Set the saddle so that, with the pedal at its lowest point, your knee keeps a slight bend.
Sit upright with both hands resting on the handlebars and your feet flat on the pedals.
Pedal at an easy resistance until your legs feel warm, then raise the resistance to where your breathing is deeper but you could still speak in full sentences.
Drop the resistance back to easy, slow your pedalling, and step off once the pedals have stopped.
cues: Keep your pedalling smooth and even rather than pushing in surges.
Sit tall rather than rounding forward over the handlebars.

exercises.name: Rowing machine
instructions: Sit on the seat, fasten the foot straps across the widest part of your feet, and take the handle with both hands.
Start with your shins upright and your arms straight, then push the floor away with your legs.
Once your legs are almost straight, lean your body back slightly and draw the handle to the bottom of your ribs.
Return in the opposite order by straightening your arms, tipping forward from your hips, then bending your knees, and hang the handle back on its hook to finish.
cues: Let your legs start the drive and your arms finish it.
Ask gym staff to watch the order of your movement the first time you use the machine.

exercises.name: Elliptical machine
instructions: Step onto the foot plates while the machine is stationary and take hold of the moving handles.
Begin at a low resistance and let the pedals travel in smooth, even circles.
Raise the resistance to where your breathing is deeper but you could still speak in full sentences, keeping your body upright.
Lower the resistance, let the pedals slow, and step off once they have stopped.
cues: Keep your whole foot in contact with the plate.
Stand tall rather than leaning your weight onto the handles.
